title: Mapping-space composition is associative and unital up to homotopy
statement:
Use small quasicategories, equivalence edges, right-pinched mapping spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a fixed sufficiently large universe. A simplicial homotopy from $r:A\to B$ to $s:A\to B$ is a map $A\times\Delta^1\to B$ restricting to $r,s$ at the endpoints; homotopy classes below use this relation for Kan targets. For a quasicategory $\mathcal D$ write $M(a,b)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(a,b)$ and let $j_{a,b}:M(a,b)\to U(a,b)$ be the specified homotopy equivalence to the arrow mapping space in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Define $V(a,b,d)$ in degree $n$ to be the maps $\Delta^2\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal D$ whose restrictions to the three vertex factors are constant at $a,b,d$, with operators by restriction in $\Delta^n$. Let $\theta:V(a,b,d)\to U(b,d)\times U(a,b)$ restrict to the edges $12,01$, in that order, and let $\ell:V(a,b,d)\to U(a,d)$ restrict to $02$. Then $V(a,b,d)$ is Kan and $\theta$ is a homotopy equivalence. The canonical composition class on the right-pinched spaces is characterized by
$$[j_{a,d}]\,c_{a,b,d}=[\ell]\,[\theta]^{-1}([j_{b,d}]\times[j_{a,b}]),\qquad c_{a,b,d}:M(b,d)\times M(a,b)\longrightarrow M(a,d).$$
These canonical composition classes are associative and unital up to simplicial homotopy: for four vertices $a,b,d,e$, the two composites from $M(d,e)\times M(b,d)\times M(a,b)$ to $M(a,e)$ are homotopic, and composing either side with the vertex represented by a degenerate identity edge is homotopic to the identity map. On components they give an ordinary category $h\mathcal D$ whose objects are the vertices and whose morphisms are $\pi_0M(a,b)$, with identities represented by degenerate edges. Every component is represented by an edge, and a $2$-simplex with edges $u:a\to b$, $v:b\to d$, $w:a\to d$ gives $[v][u]=[w]$. An edge $u:a\to b$ has invertible component class if and only if there is an edge $v:b\to a$ and $2$-simplices with boundary triples $(u,v,\mathrm{id}_a)$ and $(v,u,\mathrm{id}_b)$; thus it is precisely an equivalence edge in the definition cited above. Precomposition and postcomposition by an edge are restrictions of this canonical composition class to its vertex; they depend only on its component class.

Definition 1.4.6.1 and Remarks 1.4.6.6 and 1.4.6.8 identify invertibility with inverse-triangle witnesses. The right-pinched model and its specified inclusion are those of lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison. These are Kerodon references, not Stacks tags. Read online; archive WANTED in report.md.
